newsitem.title: USA: Clock running, FBI says Williams denied Espy role.
newsitem.headline: Clock running, FBI says Williams denied Espy role.

text.p: U.S. District Judge James Robertson employed a timeclock Wednesday to ensure a rapid trial of lobbyist Jack Williams, accused of false statements in an investigation of former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.

FBI agent Gregory Parsons said that Williams denied during a June 9, 1994, interview that he knew anything about Espy's trip to a pro football game in Dallas. Two Agriculture Department investigators gave similar testimony earlier.

Espy and his girlfriend, Patricia Dempsey, were guests of Tyson Foods, whom Williams represented, at the Jan 16, 1994, game. Other witnesses said Williams paid for Dempsey's $1,0009 ticket and advised Tyson headquarters when she would arrive.

Following through on an admonition to lawyers at the end of Tuesday's session, Robertson brought a "chess clock" to the courtroom Wednesday and told each side they had a limited amount of time to make its case.
"After seven hours, this case is over," Robertson said.
Williams told FBI agents that he could not help them, Parsons testified, and "that at the time of the game, he didn't know anything about Mr Espy's attendance."
Defense attorney Barry Levine said an FBI memo, written by Parsons and another agent, were not precise and that the FBI could have tape-recorded the interview for accuracy.
"Your notes of the interview are not verbatim, are they?" he asked Parsons.
With the Agriculture Department investigators, Levine suggested they failed to explore Williams' knowledge or do more than cursory questioning.
